dossiers.title: BURIED STARS
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The main interaction is repeatedly selecting conversational keywords and topics with a small group of survivors, extracting clues and occasionally making deductions rather than freely investigating a large environment.
Dialogue decisions affect relationships and the protagonist's sanity; accumulated clues, rapport and route-specific choices govern events and access to alternate endings.
Multiple routes and endings invite replay, but route prerequisites and the absence of an effective read-only dialogue skip make revisiting long passages cumbersome.
Repeatedly asking similar topics of the same characters often extends playtime and disrupts the suspense, particularly early and on repeat runs.
Players repeatedly appreciate the emotionally layered, flawed cast and the social-media/fame pressure woven into the central murder mystery.
The illustrated presentation, Korean performances and moody audio give character-driven scenes a memorable atmosphere.

English dialogue wording sometimes obscures the intended tone of choices and character reactions; this is a reported translation and interpretation difficulty, not a verified claim about the current build.
Progress relies more on identifying the appropriate conversational implications and clue combinations than on frequent free-form detective puzzles; some route triggers can feel opaque.

conflicts.statement: Players disagree on whether the intricate relationship and keyword dialogue system creates emotional tension or becomes an exhausting repetition of similar conversations.
Opinions differ on how damaging the English translation is: some find individual ambiguous choices tolerable, while others say their reading of dialogue options is substantially impaired.

dossiers.title: Streamer Life Simulator
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The first-person loop revolves around assembling a PC, setting up livestreams, playing simulated games, engaging with viewers and spending income on equipment or other activities.
Improving the streaming setup and leaving the initial poor living conditions provides a recognizable rags-to-better-equipment motivation.
Maintaining basic needs and leaving streams running for long stretches can turn daily play into repetitive upkeep or passive waiting.
The awkward physics, absurd situations and self-made streamer story are amusing to some players, even when the simulation feels deliberately crude.
Several players report a strong initial novelty that wears off when available interactions and meaningful new goals become limited after a few sessions.
Recent reports include progress loss after getting stuck and choppy play; older Russian player comments also describe bugs severe enough to threaten save progress.
Players are divided between finding the rough, low-budget sandbox entertaining and considering its many unfinished or awkward mechanics an obstacle to sustained enjoyment.
Early earnings, hardware setup, and streaming routines can be confusing or grinding before the systems become familiar.
PC performance impressions conflict: one older Russian player reported stutters while another found the game running acceptably; the historical remarks alone do not establish current performance.

conflicts.statement: The core streaming grind is viewed as rewarding progression by some and as mostly passive or repetitive work by others.
Older Russian PC player comments disagree about acceptable performance and polish, reporting both playable conditions and severe bugs.

dossiers.title: Internet Cafe Simulator 2
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players describe a hands-on cafe management loop: acquiring and placing computers, consoles and arcade machines, attracting visitors, earning money and expanding the premises.
Upgrading equipment and staff produces an enjoyable early business-growth arc, though experienced players report exhausting the main unlocks unusually quickly.
Absurd celebrity customers, thugs and destructive events contribute chaotic comedy; some find that unpredictability entertaining.
Routine trash cleanup, misbehaving customers and constant interruption can become intrusive chores that undercut the cafe-building experience.
Players reported unreliable physics, objects getting knocked or lost and awkward interactions in early versions, which made room setup and operations frustrating.
Current dated player comments still report poor optimization and occasional crashes alongside enjoyment of the basic game loop.

Russian-language player feedback documents flawed translation and NPC collision issues alongside praise for the game's enjoyable expansion concept; these older observations do not prove the present localization state.
Some players regard the limited late-game activities and easy money-making as reducing the challenge after rapid initial expansion.
Early attempts to manage theft, bombs, maintenance and risky side activities add hectic pressure beyond straightforward business growth.
Several early player accounts describe shop equipment or staff disappearing on reload, making save reliability a serious historical concern whose current persistence is unverified.

conflicts.statement: The cafe-building sandbox is experienced as charmingly chaotic and funny by some players, but as buggy and poorly controlled by others.
Players differ on whether rapid progression and unlocks keep the management engaging or lead to an early sense of having seen nearly everything.
